🧭 Back to [Harvesters Overview](overview.qmd)

This page describes how **SVP Harvester** keeps track of the entities (currently: persons) it harvests on behalf of,
and how it aligns their identifiers across successive requests.

---

## Entities and alignment in SVP Harvester

In SVP Harvester, harvesting activities are always conducted on behalf of an **entity** equipped with unique
**identifiers**. An entity can be an individual, a project, a research structure, or an institution — essentially,
any unit to which publications can be attributed. Currently, the system primarily supports entities of the
**person** type.

**Identifier alignment** is the process whereby an entity is associated with multiple identifiers. These identifiers
are presumed to represent the same entity, ensuring that harvesting activities are conducted consistently across the
various sources.

> ℹ️ SVP Harvester does **not** perform identifier alignment by itself. It is up to the client system (e.g.
> crisalid-ikg) to provide correct identifiers for each submitted entity. Nevertheless, SVP Harvester **memorizes**
> the submitted entities and their identifiers (unless instructed otherwise, see
> [Identifiers safe mode](#identifiers-safe-mode)) and reuses the same alignment for subsequent harvestings of the
> same entity.

When the client system submits an entity with changed identifiers, SVP Harvester does its best to update the entity
alignment with respect to the newly provided identifiers.

> ⚠️ Sending entities with shifting and contradictory alignments to SVP Harvester can put the system into an
> inconsistent state and make the harvesting history illegible, as past harvestings are **not** retroactively
> corrected when the alignment is updated.

---

## Identifiers safe mode

This whole behavior can be disabled by setting the `identifiers_safe_mode` parameter to `true` in the request body.
In this case, SVP Harvester will not register submitted identifiers nor update existing entities.

This mode is activated by default in the harvester's graphical user interface, to prevent accidental perturbation of
the entity alignments by manually submitted test requests.

---

## Recommendations

- Always submit the same entity with the same identifiers — this ensures the legibility of the harvesting history
  and the coherency of the results.
- Adding new identifiers to an existing entity is expected client behavior. SVP Harvester handles this seamlessly
  and updates its alignment accordingly.
- Correcting alignment errors is also a common operation SVP Harvester expects to occur occasionally: this includes
  merging entities that were previously considered distinct, or removing an identifier from an entity to attach it
  to another one.

---

## Identifier conflicts

An identifier conflict occurs when the alignment of a newly submitted entity is logically incompatible with
previously submitted ones.

For example, Researcher 1 is submitted with orcid identifier A and idref identifier B:

```text
Researcher 1
|
+-- orcid identifier: A
|
+-- idref identifier: B

Researcher 2
|
+-- orcid identifier: A  <- Shared orcid identifier with Researcher 1
|
+-- idref identifier: C
```

orcid A cannot belong to both entities identified respectively by idref B and idref C. This is an **identifier
conflict**. SVP Harvester resolves it according to identifier priority rules configured in `identifiers.yml`
(see the per-harvester identifier lists in [Harvesters Overview](overview.qmd#-available-harvesters) — for
instance, [HAL](hal.qmd) gives idhal identifiers priority over orcid).

---

## Examples

The following examples use the harvester's retrieval endpoint:

```text
POST /api/v1/references/retrieval
```

### Example 1: submitting a new entity

```bash
curl -X 'POST' \
  'http://my-harvester-url/api/v1/references/retrieval' \
  -H 'accept: application/json' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
  "person": {
    "identifiers": [
      { "type": "idref", "value": "111111111" },
      { "type": "orcid", "value": "0000-0001-1111-1112" }
    ],
    "name": "Smith, P"
  },
  "identifiers_safe_mode": false,
  "harvesters": ["hal", "idref", "scanr", "openalex"],
  "events": ["created", "updated", "deleted", "unchanged"]
}'
```

During the execution of this request, SVP Harvester will:

- register a new entity with the name "Smith, P" and the identifiers `111111111` (idref) and `0000-0001-1111-1112`
  (orcid)
- submit the entity to the harvesters `hal`, `idref`, `scanr` and `openalex`
- return a URL where the status and results of the harvesting can be fetched asynchronously

When a later request is submitted using **either** the idref identifier `111111111` **or** the orcid identifier
`0000-0001-1111-1112`, SVP Harvester recognizes and aligns with the previously established entity without creating
a new one — after an entity has been initially aligned with specific identifiers, subsequent retrievals require
**only one of the identifiers**, not all, to trigger a retrieval with all associated identifiers.

### Example 2: change in identifiers alignment

Following the previous example, the client system now wants to update the orcid identifier of the entity identified
by `111111111`:

```bash
curl -X 'POST' \
  'http://my-harvester-url/api/v1/references/retrieval' \
  -H 'accept: application/json' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
  "person": {
    "identifiers": [
      { "type": "idref", "value": "111111111" },
      { "type": "orcid", "value": "0000-0001-1111-1113" }
    ],
    "name": "Smith, P"
  },
  "identifiers_safe_mode": false,
  "harvesters": ["hal", "idref", "scanr", "openalex"],
  "events": ["created", "updated", "deleted", "unchanged"]
}'
```

SVP Harvester will update the entity identified by `111111111` with the new orcid identifier
`0000-0001-1111-1113`, then submit it to the requested harvesters as before.

### Example 3: identifiers safe mode

Following example 1, imagine the client system wants to submit the same idref identifier with a *different* orcid
identifier, but this time with `identifiers_safe_mode` set to `true`:

```bash
curl -X 'POST' \
  'http://my-harvester-url/api/v1/references/retrieval' \
  -H 'accept: application/json' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
  "person": {
    "identifiers": [
      { "type": "idref", "value": "111111111" },
      { "type": "orcid", "value": "0000-0001-1111-1114" }
    ],
    "name": "Smith, P"
  },
  "identifiers_safe_mode": true,
  "harvesters": ["hal", "idref", "scanr", "openalex"],
  "events": ["created", "updated", "deleted", "unchanged"]
}'
```

SVP Harvester retrieves the previously registered entity identified by `111111111` (a superior priority is given to
the idref identifier). Because `identifiers_safe_mode` is `true`, the entity is **not** updated: the newly submitted
orcid is ignored, and the entity is submitted to the harvesters with the same identifiers as in Example 1
(orcid `0000-0001-1111-1112`).

### Example 4: identifier conflict

This time the new request contains an identifier conflict: a new entity is submitted with the same orcid identifier
as an existing entity, but a different idref identifier.

```bash
curl -X 'POST' \
  'http://my-harvester-url/api/v1/references/retrieval' \
  -H 'accept: application/json' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
  "person": {
    "identifiers": [
      { "type": "idref", "value": "222222222" },
      { "type": "orcid", "value": "0000-0001-1111-1112" }
    ],
    "name": "Dupont, G"
  },
  "identifiers_safe_mode": false,
  "harvesters": ["hal", "idref", "scanr", "openalex"],
  "events": ["created", "updated", "deleted", "unchanged"]
}'
```

Since `identifiers_safe_mode` is `false`, SVP Harvester will:

- register a new entity "Dupont, G" with identifiers `222222222` (idref) and `0000-0001-1111-1112` (orcid)
- **remove** the orcid identifier `0000-0001-1111-1112` from the entity previously identified by `111111111`,
  leaving it with only its idref identifier
- submit the new entity to the requested harvesters
